key_results: CKF-Kriging-ANN achieved 99% spatial coverage with minimal redundancy; reduced sensors from 5 to 3 for temperature/moisture/pH (40% reduction), 5 to 4 for phosphorus (20% reduction); outperformed GA/PSO
comments: Two-phase Deploy-Learn-Optimize framework integrating CKF dynamics with geostatistical kriging is elegant; validation on single 8.5-hectare cassava field limits generalizability.

model_io.model: Cubature Kalman Filter + Kriging + ANN + Genetic Algorithm + Particle Swarm Optimization
inputs: soil measurements at 135 sampling points (0.2 m depth)

hypotheses.hypothesis: CKF-Kriging-ANN outperforms GA/PSO in optimizing sensor placement for agricultural WSN
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 99% coverage with 40% sensor reduction for temperature/moisture/pH

title: Deep learning-based islanding strategy for DER microgrids using a hybrid ResNet-BiGRU model optimized by an improved white-faced capuchin algorithm
task: Islanding detection in DER microgrids via deep learning with hybrid ResNet-BiGRU model
key_results: 98.2% accuracy; MSE reduced by 0.07%; RMSE reduced by 0.148% vs. baselines
comments: Improved white-faced capuchin optimization for hyperparameter tuning is novel, though marginal RMSE/MSE improvements and limited cross-dataset validation weaken claims.

model_io.model: ResNet-BiGRU-Self-Attention (RBG-SA) with IWCOA hyperparameter optimization

hypotheses.hypothesis: RBG-SA with IWCOA optimization distinguishes islanding from fault events better than baseline methods
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 98.2% accuracy; reduced MSE and RMSE

title: SSRGAT: integrating syntactic, semantic, and contextual knowledge in a knowledge-infused graph model for aspect-based sentiment analysis
task: Aspect-based sentiment analysis with multi-source knowledge integration
key_results: SSRGAT enhanced performance over competing approaches; improved accuracy and robustness on benchmark datasets
comments: Syntactic, semantic, and contextual knowledge fusion via gating mechanism is principled, but quantitative improvements over baselines not explicitly stated in abstract.

model_io.model: SSRGAT (semantic tree + graph node embeddings + gating mechanism + cross-attention)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integrating syntactic, semantic, and contextual knowledge improves aspect-sentiment accuracy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: enhanced performance and robustness on benchmarks

title: Robust vehicle re-identification with hierarchical visual refinement and conditional side-information calibration
task: Vehicle re-identification with hierarchical visual refinement and conditional side-information calibration
key_results: SCGF-Net achieved 85.9% mAP, 98.4% Rank-1, 99.2% Rank-5 on VeRi-776; improved over Swin baseline by 7.0%, 4.2%, 1.6% respectively; 2.6%, 3.4%, 3.9% improvements on VeRi-Wild transfer
comments: Hierarchical refinement (middle → high-level) with conditional residual calibration handles incomplete metadata; robustness under metadata perturbation is well-validated.

model_io.model: SCGF-Net: hierarchical visual refinement + gated fusion + conditional residual calibration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hierarchical visual refinement with conditional side-information calibration improves vehicle re-identification under dataset shift
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 85.9% mAP (VeRi-776); 2.6% mAP improvement on transfer (VeRi-Wild)

title: Interpretable modeling for material transportation process in an industrial cement vertical roller mill
task: Model material transport in industrial cement vertical roller mill via explainable machine learning
key_results: CatBoost achieved R²≈0.97 for fan speed, R²≈0.95 for fan power; SHAP analysis revealed ventilation and pressure variables as dominant drivers; identified nonlinear interactions
comments: Conscious Lab framework with CatBoost + nested cross-validation + SHAP provides interpretable process modeling; findings support real-time control strategy development.

model_io.model: CatBoost + XGBoost + Random Forest ensemble with SHAP explainability
inputs: 1050 operating records from Tehran Cement Plant; differential pressure, grinding pressures, water injection, feed variables

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ensemble ML with SHAP explainability accurately models ventilation-transport relationships in VRM circuits
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CatBoost R²=0.97 (speed), R²=0.95 (power); ventilation variables identified as dominant

title: Knowledge-guided reinforcement learning for self-adaptive software engineering and multi-objective quality optimization
task: Self-adaptive software engineering with knowledge-guided reinforcement learning
key_results: RL-SEF outperforms traditional and standalone learning-based methods; improvements in performance, reliability, and maintainability metrics with reduced adaptation time
comments: Knowledge-RL bidirectional integration and multi-objective reward adjustment are conceptually sound, but abstract lacks quantitative performance metrics for comparison.

model_io.model: RL-SEF: RL agent + domain knowledge representations + knowledge-directed exploration + hybrid decision-making

hypotheses.hypothesis: Knowledge-guided RL improves software quality more than standalone RL or static knowledge approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: superior performance on quality metrics with reduced manual intervention

title: A cluster-aware XAI-MCDM framework for province-level solar PV suitability screening in Turkey using real operational PV data
task: Province-level solar PV suitability screening in Turkey via cluster-aware XAI-MCDM
key_results: ANN achieved test R²=0.782, nRMSE=11.92%; XAI identified solar-radiation as dominant predictor; MCDM ensemble identified Mersin as highest-priority national candidate; 8-province high-priority portfolio delineated
comments: Integration of operational PV data with SHAP/permutation importance for criterion weighting is novel; cluster-aware benchmarking enables regional contextualization of national rankings.

model_io.model: Leakage-controlled ANN + Multi-XAI (SHAP, permutation importance, MI, correlation) + MEREC + MCDM ensemble (MARCOS, TOPSIS, EDAS)
inputs: 47,185 hourly observations from 4 operational PV plants

hypotheses.hypothesis: Solar-radiation-based criterion weights derived from operational PV data improve suitability assessment vs. expert judgment
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ANN-XAI identified solar radiation as dominant; explainable MCDM provides province portfolio

title: A network-based known-unknown model for predicting scientific impact from topic selection strategies
task: Model research topic selection strategies and predict long-term scientific impact
key_results: Known–Unknown Model outperforms benchmarks in predicting H-index and Q-index; balanced exploration–exploitation strategies maximize sustained influence
comments: Parsimonious single-parameter model elegantly formalizes depth-breadth tradeoff, yet causal inference from observational career data remains fundamentally limited.

model_io.model: Known–Unknown Model (KUM) with binary topic-choice framework
inputs: publication data from American Physical Society (APS)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Balanced exploration–exploitation predicts greater sustained scientific influence than extreme strategies
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: superior H-index and Q-index prediction vs. conservatism or novelty-seeking

title: Hardware implementation of photonic neuromorphic autonomous navigation
task: Photonic neuromorphic autonomous navigation via reinforcement learning with hardware implementation
key_results: Average reward 58.22 ± 17.29; success rate 80% ± 8.3%; nonlinear activation energy 0.78 nJ/event; latency 191.20 ps; co-inference error rates 0.051–0.059%
comments: DFB-SA laser array hardware-software co-inference demonstrates photonic viability; low energy and latency are compelling, though navigation task complexity and generalization warrant further validation.

model_io.model: Photonic spiking twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient RL (Actor + dual Critic networks); DFB-SA laser array final activation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Photonic spiking architecture achieves autonomous navigation with low energy/latency vs. electronic implementation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 0.78 nJ/activation, 191.20 ps latency; 80% navigation success

title: Reliability challenges for resistive random-access memory-based parallel logic computing
task: Investigate reliability of resistive random-access memory-based parallel logic computing
key_results: Demonstrated parallel and cascading logic execution in RRAM CIM array; simulation study identified optimization strategies for logic accuracy and reliability
comments: Experimental validation combined with in-depth simulation provides insights into RRAM-CIM reliability; scalability and error rates for larger arrays remain open questions.

model_io.model: RRAM-based computing-in-memory array with parallel logic execution

hypotheses.hypothesis: RRAM-based CIM can reliably execute parallel and cascading logic functions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: feasibility demonstrated; optimization strategies outlined

title: The digital native fallacy: how age-based assumptions exclude young adults with chronic disease from digital health innovations
task: Examine digital native fallacy in digital health design for young adults with chronic disease
key_results: Social media fluency ≠ health literacy; digital access structurally unstable; insurance gaps exacerbate chronic disease risks; proposed five equity-first design principles
comments: US-based evidence challenges implicit assumptions in digital health; transferability to other contexts unclear; calls for equity-first rather than youth-centric design.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Digital native status does not ensure health digital competence or stable access for young chronic disease patients
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: social media fluency, access instability, and insurance gaps identified as barriers

title: Orientational enhancement of surface phonon polarity in superconducting KTaO₃ interfaces
task: Correlate surface phonon polarity with superconductivity in KTaO3 interfaces
key_results: 35-fold enhancement of phonon polarity for (111) orientation; phonon resonance near 107 meV tracks superconducting Tc
comments: Establishes symmetry-breaking lattice phonons and defects as mediators of anisotropic superconductivity, though causality versus correlation requires further investigation.

model_io.model: KTaO3-based heterointerfaces with different crystallographic orientations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Polarity of surface phonon mode scales with crystallographic orientation and tracks Tc
hypotheses.result: (111) shows 35-fold enhancement over (001); anisotropic phonon resonance near 107 meV correlates with superconducting properties

title: Selective filtering of multi-photon events from a single-photon emitter
task: Filter multi-photon errors from single-photon emitter via spectral discrimination
key_results: Reduced second-order coherence at zero delay by nearly one order of magnitude; suppressed multi-photon error rate without degrading single-photon emission
comments: Overcomes fundamental limit via spectro-temporal filtering; elegant approach though requires short driving pulses and may introduce detection efficiency trade-offs.

model_io.model: Single-photon emitter driven by short pulse with narrowband spectral filters

hypotheses.hypothesis: Instantaneously emitted multi-photons exhibit broader spectrum than natural linewidth, enabling selective filtering
hypotheses.result: Narrowband filters suppress g²(0) by ~one order of magnitude; multi-photon error rate significantly reduced without single-photon loss

title: Yu-Shiba-Rusinov-assisted Andreev transport in a molecular junction between superconductors
task: Investigate YSR-assisted Andreev reflection in molecular superconducting junction
key_results: Continuous tuning from YSR spectroscopy to resonant MAR to Josephson coupling; shifted MAR thresholds and odd-even features identified
comments: Elegant demonstration of junction transparency control enabling multiple transport regimes in a single device; antiferromagnetic Nc-Fe ground state provides clear mechanism for YSR resonances.

model_io.model: Nickelocene/Fe adatom on Pb(111) with superconducting STM tip

hypotheses.hypothesis: YSR bound states enable resonant MAR with shifted thresholds and asymmetric lineshapes
hypotheses.result: Continuous transition observed from tunneling regime to MAR transport to Josephson coupling; antiferromagnetic Nc-Fe ground state confirmed via DFT

title: Tunable arbitrarily located quasi-corner states in multiphase weak topological insulator
task: Realize tunable quasi-corner states via weak topology in anisotropic honeycomb lattices
key_results: Quasi-corner state positions tunable by uniaxial strain; three weak topological phases support three distinct localization sites; long-range coupling enables dynamic oscillation
comments: Novel weak topology mechanism for 0D states differs from established HOTI classification; however, experimental realization and observation of dynamic coupling still pending.

model_io.model: 2D anisotropic honeycomb lattice with vacancy defects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Weak topology at vacancy defects protects 0D quasi-corner states with tunable localization via strain
hypotheses.result: Three weak phases correspond to three distinct quasi-corner sites; Wannier center location at broken bond enables position tuning

title: Correlated insulating states in slow Dirac fermions on a honeycomb moiré superlattice
task: Realize Mott insulator state in graphene-like bands via moiré superlattice
key_results: Mott gap persisting to 110 K; correlated insulating states at integer and fractional fillings detected via Rydberg-exciton sensing
comments: Successfully demonstrates strong correlation physics in engineered slow Dirac fermion systems, though experimental confirmation of full SU(2) symmetry could be strengthened.

model_io.model: Twisted MoSe2 homobilayer with honeycomb moiré superlattice
inputs: Valence band maximum at Γ valley

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reduced Fermi velocity (two orders of magnitude) enables Mott insulating phase at Dirac point
hypotheses.result: Mott gap confirmed experimentally via Rydberg-exciton sensing up to 110 K

title: Isotropic-carrier-transport perovskite single crystal enables high-photoresponsivity solar-blind photodetectors for selective flame monitoring
task: Enable high-photoresponsivity solar-blind UV detectors using 3D perovskite CsCdCl3 single crystals
key_results: Photoresponsivity 35.4 A/W; dark current 1.0×10⁻¹² A; narrowband spectral response (20 nm) with rejection ratio 1.96×10³; flame selectivity demonstrated
comments: Impressive performance via isotropic carrier transport in 3D framework; 20 nm spectral resolution excellent for selective flame monitoring applications.

model_io.model: CsCdCl3 perovskite single-crystal solar-blind photodetector

hypotheses.hypothesis: 3D structural framework with isotropic carrier transport enables high photoresponsivity and low dark current
hypotheses.result: CsCdCl3 achieves 35.4 A/W responsivity and 1.0×10⁻¹² A dark current; narrowband response enables flame-type discrimination

title: Microscopic screening theory for excitons in two-dimensional materials: a bridge between effective models and ab initio descriptions
task: Develop microscopic screening theory for exciton binding energies in 2D materials via BSE
key_results: Quantum screened interactions via random-phase approximation dielectric function; realistic binding energy estimates with ab initio accuracy at modest computational cost
comments: Bridges effective models and first-principles via explicit screening; convergence analysis addresses literature dispersion in binding energies reported by GW/BSE.

model_io.model: Bethe–Salpeter equation with atomistic description and quantum screened interactions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit quantum screening at RPA level yields realistic binding energies comparable to first-principles with lower cost
hypotheses.result: Method captures screening beyond Rytova–Keldysh model; convergence analysis identifies sources of literature dispersion in binding energies

title: Layer-engineered quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted rhombohedral graphene
task: Realize programmable topological states via layer-engineered quantum anomalous Hall effect
key_results: Chern number C = N programmable by layer number (N=3,4,5); electrical tuning of C sign and displacement-field-induced phase transitions (C=3↔C=4)
comments: Elegant layer engineering establishes C as programmable degree of freedom; on-demand topological state engineering demonstrated though experimental control robustness deserves scrutiny.

model_io.model: Twisted monolayer-multilayer rhombohedral graphene with electric/displacement field control

hypotheses.hypothesis: Layer number N directly sets Chern number C=N in twisted rhombohedral graphene stacks
hypotheses.result: QAH states with C=3,4,5 realized; C sign switched electrically; displacement-field-induced phase transitions between C=3 and C=4 demonstrated

title: Point-like photovoltaic junction in 2D semiconductor homobilayer
task: Probe point-like photovoltaic junctions via nanoscale photoresponse in 2D semiconductor homobilayer
key_results: Nanometre-scale photocurrent hotspots centered on single dopants; linear macroscopic scaling with dopant concentration; dopant-defined junctions enable ~1 nm exciton dissociation
comments: Novel dopant-localized photovoltaic mechanism in atomically thin materials; dopant-defined point junctions generalize beyond WSe2 for topological material studies.

model_io.model: V-doped WSe2 bilayer with photoconductive AFM and vertical device geometry

hypotheses.hypothesis: Single dopant acceptors locally convert tightly bound intralayer excitons into charge-separated interlayer states within ~1 nm
hypotheses.result: AFM reveals dopant-centered photocurrent hotspots; macroscopic current scales linearly with dopant density independent of illumination power

title: Quantum Hall antidot as a fractional coulombmeter
task: Measure fractional charge via quasiparticle tunneling through bilayer-graphene antidot
key_results: Direct measurement of fractional charge in fractional quantum Hall states; charge variations attributed to edge re-equilibration from mode parity differences
comments: Elegant application of antidots for charge measurement; design tunability promising for van der Waals materials, though charge measurement precision limited by edge-mode complexity.

model_io.model: Gate-defined bilayer-graphene antidot in Coulomb-dominated regime

hypotheses.hypothesis: Measured fractional charge depends on edge mode parity due to re-equilibration differences
hypotheses.result: Direct charge measurements confirm fractional values; charge variation explained by downstream integer edge mode parity

title: Response of the peeled off Gafchromic EBT2 film to 4 MeV alpha particles using transmission and reflection modes
task: Characterize spatial resolution and dose response of peeled-off Gafchromic EBT2 film to 4 MeV alpha particles
key_results: Transmission mode exhibits higher Weber contrast increase with dose than reflection; green channel yields highest spatial resolution in both modes; FWHM shows dose-independence in transmission
comments: Practical dosimetry study with detailed mode comparison; transmission mode preferred for dose measurements though reflection mode may offer dose-response consistency benefits.

model_io.model: Peeled-off Gafchromic EBT2 film irradiated with 4 MeV alpha particles and scanned in transmission/reflection modes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transmission mode provides superior dose-response linearity and stable spatial resolution independent of dose
hypotheses.result: Weber contrast increases more rapidly in transmission mode; FWHM dose-independent in transmission but slightly correlated in reflection; green channel optimal

title: Quantum magnetometry with superconducting-qubit Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger and Dicke probes
task: Compare GHZ and Dicke entangled states for quantum magnetometry in superconducting qubits
key_results: GHZ probes achieve highest local sensitivity; Dicke probes maintain comparable sensitivity over wider bias interval with improved noise robustness
comments: Systematic comparison under realistic noise well-motivated; trade-off between peak sensitivity and dynamical range is practically valuable for device design.

model_io.model: Fluxonium-qubit sensors with GHZ or Dicke probes in Kitaev phase estimation algorithm

hypotheses.hypothesis: GHZ states achieve peak sensitivity with reduced dynamical range; Dicke states trade local sensitivity for robustness
hypotheses.result: GHZ exhibits highest local sensitivity but narrower bias interval; Dicke maintains comparable sensitivity over wider range with better noise tolerance

title: Effect of sputtering power on the optoelectrical performance and mechanical durability of AZO thin films
task: Optimize AZO thin films for balanced optoelectrical performance and mechanical durability
key_results: Visible transmittance 76–84%; conductivity loss under tribological loading reduced from 2×10⁴ to 4×10⁴ cycles; hardness 6.2–7.3 GPa
comments: Practical multi-criteria optimization via sputtering power; highest PE/PC ratio (400/200 W/W) offers best wear resistance though transmittance-conductivity trade-off inherent.

model_io.model: AZO thin film deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering at varying PE/PC ratios

hypotheses.hypothesis: Increasing PE/PC ratio improves transparency and wear resistance while maintaining conductivity
hypotheses.result: Transmittance increases from 76% to 84%; wear resistance improved from 2×10⁴ to 4×10⁴ cycles at highest PE/PC ratio

title: A compact 4-port asymmetric open-slot MIMO antenna for smartwatch-integrated Wi-Fi applications
task: Design compact 4-port MIMO antenna for smartwatch Wi-Fi with high isolation and diversity
key_results: Isolation ~−20 dB (5.15–5.85 GHz); ECC ≈0.01; diversity gain ≈9.999 dB; channel capacity loss <0.4 bits/s/Hz
comments: Practical engineering design with good measured-simulation agreement; however, performance metrics are standard for modern MIMO and lack novelty in topology.

model_io.model: FR4 substrate 4-port antenna with asymmetric elements and DGS

hypotheses.hypothesis: Asymmetric element configuration and DGS reduce inter-element coupling to achieve −20 dB isolation
hypotheses.result: Measured isolation ~−20 dB confirmed; ECC 0.01 and DG 9.999 dB demonstrate excellent diversity performance

title: Ferroelectric spintronics in van der Waals materials
task: Realize ferroelectric spintronic control via polarization switching in van der Waals materials
key_results: Sliding ferroelectricity enables ultralow polarization switching barriers; FESO devices combine polarization control with Rashba-Edelstein and spin Hall effects
comments: Perspective on emerging 2D vdW ferroelectrics for spintronics; sliding mechanism overcomes ultrathin-film instabilities though device implementation challenges remain substantial.

model_io.model: 2D van der Waals ferroelectric with interlayer displacement and spin-orbit coupling

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sliding ferroelectricity enables efficient nonvolatile polarization control of spin textures via reduced switching barriers
hypotheses.result: vdW ferroelectrics overcome ultrathin-film polarization instabilities; polarization-controlled SCC and spin-orbit responses demonstrated via sliding mechanism

title: Asymmetric edge supercurrents in topological PdTe2 Josephson junctions
task: Identify higher-order topological states via edge supercurrents in PdTe2 Josephson junctions
key_results: Edge supercurrents increase more rapidly with decreasing temperature than bulk/surface supercurrents; asymmetric hinge state model confirmed
comments: Convincing evidence for higher-order topology in PdTe2, though the distinction between edge and hinge contributions could benefit from additional spectroscopic characterization.

model_io.model: Nb-PdTe2-Nb Josephson junctions with edge-touched and edge-untouched configurations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nontrivial higher-order edge states exhibit temperature-dependent supercurrent distinct from bulk
hypotheses.result: Edge supercurrent increases more rapidly with decreasing T; asymmetric hinge state model supported by first-principles calculations

title: Boundaries of acceptable defectiveness: redefining surface code robustness under heterogeneous noise
task: Define boundaries of acceptable defectiveness for surface code under heterogeneous noise
key_results: Defective qubits (error rate ≤0.75) tolerated with negligible logical impact at sufficient code distance and proper placement; Gaussian noise deviation has minimal effect
comments: Practical framework for realistic device design with imperfect qubits; heterogeneity resilience valuable though optimal placement strategy complexity understated.

model_io.model: Rotated surface code with parametric noise model and qubit defects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Defective qubits with error rate ≤0.75 can be tolerated if placed appropriately and code distance sufficiently large
hypotheses.result: Logical error rate shows minimal impact from individual defects and Gaussian noise deviation; boundaries of acceptable defectiveness defined quantitatively

title: Lattice random walk discretisations of stochastic differential equations
task: Discretize stochastic differential equations via binary/ternary lattice random walk sampling
key_results: Weak convergence proven; eliminates Gaussian sampling and floating-point arithmetic; robust to quantization errors and handles non-Lipschitz drifts
comments: Significant departure from traditional discretization with advantages for stochastic computing; weak convergence analysis rigorous though strong convergence rate not addressed.

model_io.model: Lattice random walk discretization scheme for SDEs with binary/ternary increments

hypotheses.hypothesis: Binary/ternary increment sampling achieves weak convergence while avoiding floating-point and Gaussian sampling complexities
hypotheses.result: Weak convergence proven; experiments validate advantages on various SDEs including state-of-the-art diffusion models
